risk: Block-internal n-1 cannot be removed by any filtration mode; final full-length purity is floored at the product of block full-length fractions.
mitigation: Control at creation: high block full-length purity + high ligation conversion. Block-stage IEX/RP polishing (at supplier, on short blocks where 1 nt is easier to resolve). Accept a single final strand polish only if DS spec exceeds the achievable floor.
notes: Core of finding 1. Confirmed by A, B, C+D.

risk: Immobilised-ligase clearance by filtration is unproven at scale; if it fails, enzyme removal reverts to chromatography (affinity/IEX), breaking the filtration-led thesis.
mitigation: Develop and qualify immobilised or solid-phase ligase with measured residual-protein clearance; keep a chromatographic enzyme-removal fallback in the concept.
notes: No public ppm/log clearance data (Q-032, now restated as NOT PUBLICLY AVAILABLE rather than 'not yet found'). Immobilisation holds conversion (>92%, SRC-CN119265174) but the CN patent still heat-kills and runs an ion column, so it does not by itself deliver a chromatography-free train.

risk: Duplex may dissociate or degrade during atomisation/drying if particle temperature approaches the melting temperature.
mitigation: Keep the powder below its MOISTURE-SHIFTED glass transition (measured 38-53 C at 3.8-4.6% residual moisture), which binds BEFORE the duplex melting temperature (58-64 C); drive residual moisture down to raise Tg. Keep outlet below Tm as the looser limit. Trehalose amorphous glass; N2 low-oxygen drying. Fallback: dry single strands separately and anneal downstream.
notes: REFOCUSED on temperature and the glass transition (F-003). Tg (38-53 C, SRC-KEIL-2021, Q-039) binds first; measured duplex Tm is 58-64 C (SRC-MALEK-2019, Q-030), the looser limit. Atomisation SHEAR is retired as a governing risk: naked siRNA kept >80% integrity and full activity through atomisation, while plasmid DNA did not (SRC-NAKED-NA-2023). Post-drying margin binds on storage as well as drying.

risk: Thermal degradation of product in the evaporator from residence-time x temperature.
mitigation: Short-residence type (falling/wiped/thin film, residence seconds) under vacuum to hold temperature low. At small batch the minimum wetting rate forces recirculation (R-013), so control CUMULATIVE passes x temperature, not a single pass. Avoid forced circulation.
notes: Correlations are food/fine-chemical; transferability caveat. Restated in terms of cumulative passes: below the minimum wetting rate the film breaks up, so a small batch must recirculate and multiply thermal exposure (SRC-HUGHES-2024, R-013).

risk: Non-volatile buffer salts (Tris/Mg/NaCl) concentrate through evaporation into the powder unless the final diafiltration exchanges into a spray-dry-compatible matrix.
mitigation: Final DF into excipient + minimal/volatile salt matrix (BUF-FINAL) before evaporation/drying.
notes: Hard constraint identified in audit.

risk: Splint removal would be infeasible by filtration if a foreign same-chemistry splint were used.
mitigation: Use the complementary product strand as the splint (siRNA sticky-end route); avoid a sacrificial foreign splint. If unavoidable, DNase digestion (adds a protein impurity to clear).
notes: Largely designed out for siRNA.

risk: Endotoxin clearance by membrane adsorber is unproven for a polyanionic oligonucleotide feed (product competes for charged sites).
mitigation: Low-bioburden operation, endotoxin-controlled reagents/water, hold-time limits; qualify positively-charged/guanidinium adsorbers experimentally.
notes: Top endotoxin gap. The adsorber-alone case is now tested against a competing polyanion and fell two orders short: 641 EU/mg with membrane adsorbers alone, reaching spec only with an orthogonal NaOH step at 29% recovery (SRC-DEVRIES-2018). The registered buffer-matrix study (SRC-PMC12226154) had nothing competing for the ligand - precisely the condition that will not hold for our polyanionic stream. See Q-037.

risk: Spray dryer and evaporator are hard to clean (wall deposits, cyclone product); CIP/SIP validation for low-bioburden operation is demanding.
mitigation: Design CIP/SIP with the vendor; consider single-use contact where feasible; cleaning validation with worst-case soils.
notes: Tier-2 detail; flagged now.

risk: Aqueous intermediates with growth-promoting buffers support microbial growth during holds.
mitigation: Refrigerated storage, limited hold times, bioburden-reduction filtration into sanitised vessels for extended holds; bioburden/endotoxin monitoring.
notes: Bioburden tightens 100 -> 10 CFU/10 mL toward DS.

risk: Adenylylated dead-end (AppN) species (~329 Da difference) cannot be removed by filtration.
mitigation: Enzyme/ATP selection to suppress AppN (e.g., dsRNA ligases, controlled ATP); control at reaction, not downstream.
notes: Observed in EXACTLY this chemistry: an adenylylated dead-end by-product '2.3_2.4[+AMP]' in fully modified siRNA blockmer ligation (SRC-ALMAC-2023, Table 1). The authors' mitigation was to change the disconnection and reaction staging so it does not form, not to remove it downstream - the control philosophy this risk asserts. Same separation limit as n-1. ATP tension: suppressing it wants <100 uM ATP against >=4 mM required for the assembly (Q-040).

risk: Membrane area and yield are sized on protein and plasmid-DNA surrogate flux from a weak secondary source; no oligonucleotide-specific flux or recovery figure exists.
mitigation: Measure flux, fouling and recovery on the real stream at bench and pilot scale before fixing membrane area; treat all current LMH figures as placeholders.
notes: See Q-036. The previously cited ~80% RNA recovery figure does not exist in the cited source.

risk: Microbial and endotoxin limits in this knowledge base are carried over from mammalian cell-culture practice and are unverified for an oligonucleotide drug substance.
mitigation: Obtain the oligonucleotide-specific microbiological control paper and replace the ladder; until then do not use these numbers as specifications.
notes: CLOSED (F-006). Every figure on the old microbial ladder was located verbatim in a mammalian cell-culture article, hedged there as typical practice (SRC-BPI-HOLDTIME-2025). The ladder has been removed; the oligonucleotide-specific bioburden figure (<1 CFU/mL, SRC-PMC7415879) and a dose-derived endotoxin limit replace it. See Q-037.

risk: Falling-film minimum wetting rate makes the evaporator turndown-limited: a small batch cannot run single-pass and must recirculate, multiplying cumulative thermal exposure.
mitigation: Size the evaporator on minimum wetting rate (0.10-0.22 kg/m/s for water, ~57-65 kg/h for one 48 mm tube); at small batch expect recirculation and control cumulative passes (R-004). A rotary evaporator is not a scale-down model of a falling film.
notes: Below the minimum wetting rate the film breaks into rivulets and dry patches foul - a heat-transfer failure, not a throughput inconvenience (SRC-HUGHES-2024, reporting SRC-MORISON-2006). Values are for water on steel, NOT a polyelectrolyte solution; transfer is plausible but unproven. Perimeter/feed arithmetic is ours (INFERENCE). See Q-018, R-004.

risk: Magnesium and calcium bind the polyanion and can block impurity passage in diafiltration; the ligation buffer contains magnesium chloride.
mitigation: Exchange divalent cations out early; verify that cationic and divalent impurities actually clear the membrane on the real stream rather than assuming they diafilter like monovalent salts.
notes: A polyanion will not diafilter out cationic impurities 'even for common divalent cations such as calcium or magnesium' (SRC-GRONKE-2023, single-strand antisense - the mechanism transfers). BUF-LIG carries MgCl2. See Q-020, Q-036.

risk: No health-based exposure limit (HBEL) exists anywhere in the registers for cleaning validation of shared filtration and drying equipment.
mitigation: Derive an HBEL for a potent, highly water-soluble polyanion and write a cleaning-validation master plan against worst-case soils on the evaporator and dryer (the hardest-to-clean items).
notes: A cleaning-validation master plan with health-based exposure limits is a named technology-transfer deliverable (SRC-WHO-TRS1044) and is absent here. Compounds R-008 (hard-to-clean evaporator/dryer). See Q-043.

risk: Dust explosion on the spray dryer, cyclone and powder receiver handling a dried organic drug substance.
mitigation: Apply the current combustible-dust standard (NFPA 660-2025, which consolidated NFPA 654) with explosion protection (NFPA 68/69). The explosion parameters of the actual powder (Kst, MIE, MEC) are a TESTING deliverable, not a literature lookup.
notes: A spray-dried powder brings the combustible-dust standard into scope (SRC-STANDARDS-CURRENT). Not previously registered. See the facility page.

risk: Published ligation routes feed cell-free extract, so the protein burden entering purification is a whole proteome plus endotoxin, not a single ligase.
mitigation: Prefer purified or immobilised enzyme over cell-free extract; if extract is used, size protein and endotoxin clearance against a whole-proteome load, not one enzyme.
notes: The demonstrated modified-siRNA route uses an RNA-ligase/PNK cell-free extract at 1 mg/mL (SRC-ALMAC-2023, SI). That raises the clearance burden behind R-002 and R-007 well above a single ligase. See Q-032.

risk: A block route that omits capping converts coupling failures into block-internal deletions (n-1) rather than truncations - the class filtration cannot remove.
mitigation: Preserve capping at the block stage where possible, or control block full-length purity tightly, since internal deletions propagate to the product and cannot be cleared downstream (R-001).
notes: Capping in solid-phase synthesis converts coupling failures into truncated sequences and minimises n-1 (SRC-IQ-SUSTAIN-2021). A liquid-phase block route that drops it converts the same failures into block-internal n-1 - the harder class (INFERENCE, ours). Core of R-001. See Q-011.

risk: No demonstrated chromatography-free ligation drug-substance train exists in the public record; both named commercial routes end in HPLC purification of the siRNA itself.
mitigation: Treat the filtration-only final step as unproven and stage a per-strand chromatographic polish as the retained fallback; demonstrate the chromatography-free step at pilot before committing.
notes: Both named routes are HPLC-purified at the siRNA level: 'P-to-P = HPLC purified fragments and purified siRNA; C-to-P = UF/DF processed fragments and HPLC purified siRNA' on ~960 g and ~1020 g GMP batches (SRC-HONGENE-BROCHURE-2025). Filtration replaces FRAGMENT chromatography, not final-product chromatography. The site is ahead of demonstrated practice at the final-purification step; this is not an argument to change the process. See the filtration finding S7.

risk: The 'oligonucleotides are intrinsically low-bioburden' argument does not apply: it assumes solvent synthesis and a single aqueous step, and this fully aqueous enzymatic route with an enzyme and buffer in the stream has neither.
mitigation: Build the contamination-control strategy from this process's own risk (aqueous throughout, enzyme + growth-promoting buffer, holds), not inherited from the modality; set bioburden and endotoxin specifications on the drug substance.
notes: The published low-bioburden rationale has exactly two premises - solvent synthesis, only the last step aqueous - and neither holds here (SRC-PMC7415879). Reason a CCS is needed rather than assumed. See Q-037, Q-043, R-009.
